submitted.rationale: Index 11 (Bi 0.466, V 0.534) gave the highest photocurrent, 2.17e-5 A. At this composition the film is slightly V-rich monoclinic BiVO4. MACE puts that phase on the hull (0.008 eV/atom) and MEGNet predicts an HSE gap of 2.81 eV, below the 3.22 eV photon energy. The Bi-rich side collapses: index 8 (Bi 0.53) gave 1.6e-7 A. That fits the Bi-rich phases absorbing poorly, since Bi4V2O11 has a predicted gap of 3.76 eV. Going further V-rich (index 4, Bi 0.31) gave 1.73e-5 A, so the peak lies close to index 11.

rejected.reason: Measured 1.6e-7 A, about 100x lower. Bi-rich films form wide-gap Bi4V2O11 or Bi-rich phases.
Measured 1.73e-5 A, below index 11. The extra vanadium oxide dilutes the BiVO4.
Not measured. Its composition is nearly the same as index 11 (Bi 0.457), so it would have told us little.

consultations.verdict: Support: BiVO4 (mp-23044) is near-hull (0.008 eV/atom) with HSE gap 2.81 eV < 3.22 eV photon energy, so compositions near Bi:V=1:1 should form the active BiVO4 photoanode phase. Index 11 (Bi 0.466) is slightly V-rich, typically favorable.

Mixed/support for 8: Bi4V2O11 (the Bi-rich neighbor phase) has HSE gap 3.76 eV > 3.22 eV, so Bi-rich compositions (Bi≥0.6) will absorb poorly; index 8 (Bi 0.53) is still dominated by absorbing BiVO4, so it's the best test of the Bi-rich side of the 1:1 peak.

Weak support: the only V-rich ternary (BiV2O2) is far off hull (1.05 eV/atom), so V-rich films are BiVO4 + vanadium oxide, still containing the absorbing BiVO4 phase. Measured data show a steep drop on the Bi-rich side (0.53: 1.6e-7 A vs 0.466: 2.2e-5 A), so the optimum likely lies on the V-rich side; index 4 (Bi 0.31) tests that with no downside to the max-based score.
